title: Observability pocket notes
content:
Quick pocket notes for today's console triage (grab-and-run). Informal, will flesh out later.

2026-03-13 09:10 — morning sweep
- Dashboard: 'svc-token-service / request-latency' p95 spike around 09:02, p99 up to ~2.1s (baseline 450ms).
- KV cache miss rate on redux-cache-prod up ~3x from baseline between 08:50–09:05. correlates with rolling restart (kube events show restart loop on node gpu-7).
- Alert noisy: CPU throttling alert fired twice then auto-resolved. Looks like k8s HPA flapping.
- Customer report: CS-4721 — "slow response for embeddings at 09:00-09:10, timed out on retries". Customer attached trace id: trace:577a3c2f.

First-pass hypotheses
- Rolling restart on gpu-7 caused temporary cache warmup + KV misses, pushing synchronous requests to slower fallback model variant -> latency spike.
- HPA/cpu throttle flapping likely separate but may have amplified congestion on a subset of pods.

Immediate actions taken (done)
- Patched alert thresholds on "svc-token-service-p95" to reduce immediate noise (temporary). // cmd I ran: kubectl get pods -n prod | grep token-service && kubectl describe pod token-service-7b9f -n prod
- Re-ran quick KV cache health query: curl -s 'https://internal-api.redwood/kv/metrics?env=prod' | jq '.miss_rate' -> confirmed spike then decay after 09:12
- Notified infra on #infra-gpu: "gpu-7 showing OOM-ish restart pattern, candidate for cordon/reimage" (pinged Ethan).

Open items / follow-ups
- [ ] Confirm whether model fallback happened automatically for requests during 09:00-09:15; check router logs for fallback events (route: /v1/generate, model: rw-3b-quant). Linked to OBS-1284.
- [ ] Ask platform eng to look at node gpu-7 event logs and kubelet errors; if recurring, schedule reimage. (Marta assigned)
- [ ] Clean up HPA config for token-service; investigate why CPU request -> throttle -> flapping HPA scale-up/scale-down. Possibly misconfigured metrics. (assign to #sre-oncall)
- [ ] Add a tiny health-check on KV cache warm path to catch cache warmup early (proposal: synthetic short seq requests routed once per minute).
- [ ] Draft short note for CS to explain root cause and mitigation; include trace id and timeline. (Nadia)

Notes for debug (quick commands, copyable)
- Check router fallbacks: 
  curl -s 'https://logs.internal/api/search?q=router.fallback%20trace:577a3c2f' | jq '.hits'
- KV cache metrics by pod: 
  kubectl -n prod exec $(kubectl -n prod get pod -l app=redux-cache -o name | head -1) -- curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep cache_miss
- Pod restart history on node gpu-7: 
  kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Node,involvedObject.name=gpu-7 --all-namespaces --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 50

Customer communication draft (short)
- "We've identified a transient backend degradation tied to a node restart and concurrent autoscaling events that increased cache miss rates and caused a small fraction of requests to fall back to slower model variants between 09:00–09:15. We have remediated by stabilizing the affected node and tuning autoscaling; full postmortem will follow. Trace id: 577a3c2f. Apologies for the disruption."

Ideas / low-effort mitigations to try this week
- Add tracer-level sampling on router so fallbacks show up in customer-facing trace link (helpful for CS).
- Create a short-runbook snippet for "KV warmup after node restart" with mitigation steps: cordon, drain, pre-warm cache, uncordon.
- Experiment: increase KV cache pre-warm window on graceful drain to reduce miss spike.

Loose dayplan (my TODOs)
- 09:30–10:15: dig router logs for fallback events + annotate timeline -> update OBS-1284.
- 10:30: sync with Marta (infra) on node health / possible reimage.
- 11:00: prepare note for CS (CS-4721) and post on the ticket.
- Afternoon: quick spike to prototype KV pre-warm synthetic request in staging and run it on a node restart cycle.

Random / scratch bits (phone numbers, pings, quick thoughts)
- Slack pings: @ethan (infra), @marta (infra), @lius (platform), @sarah-cs (CS lead)
- If we see repeat: consider routing policy change to prefer model-variant-resident pods when KV miss rate > X%
- Q: do we have historical baseline for KV miss spikes after node restarts? If not, add metric and baseline it (V2 work).

End of pocket notes — will flesh into OBS-1284 doc + CS reply later.
